segments.text: Sorry, doctor, sorry, I'm very late. There was a traffic jam near the flyover, and then the auto driver took the wrong turn, and then I could not find the clinic entrance.
Please, don't worry about it. You've made it, that's what matters. Sit down and tell me what brought you in.
So, it is about my periods, doctor. I'm having bleeding between my periods, since last two months. It was never like this before.
Okay. Can you describe what it looks like, and how much there is?

Mostly it is only spotting, light pink or brown, on the underwear. But last week it was little more, I had to use a pad for two days. I was so worried, I told my husband, he said just go and see the doctor.
You did the right thing. When do you notice the bleeding, in relation to your regular period?

About ten days after my period finishes. Then again some days later, on and off. My cycle is usually regular, you know, twenty-eight days like a clock. My sister always says I'm the only person who is regular in our family.
That's helpful to know. Any pain along with it?
Yes, some pain in my lower tummy, like a dull ache, mild only. It comes with the bleeding, mostly. I thought maybe it is gas, because last Sunday we had my aunt's biryani and I ate too much.
Mm. And is the ache on one side or all across the lower tummy?
All across, I think. Not one side. It is not so bad, I can still do my work.
Good. Now I need to ask a few things you might find personal, so please say if you'd like a break. Have you had any bleeding after intercourse?
No, no, nothing like that. That is fine.
Any fever, or chills, along with these symptoms?
No fever. I checked also with the thermometer, because my mother-in-law was after me about it.
And is there any chance that you might be pregnant at the moment?
No chance, doctor. We are being careful, and my last period was normal, on time.
Alright. Tell me about your health in general. Any longer-term conditions I should know about?
Only the PCOS. Polycystic ovary syndrome, they said, long back. But my periods have been regular, so I stopped worrying about it. That is why this is so strange for me.
Okay, that's good to have on record. Anything in the way of operations or procedures?
I had a C-section, four years ago. For my daughter. She is four now, and she is the naughtiest, doctor, you won't believe it. Yesterday she painted the dog with my lipstick.
That sounds like a handful. Is life busy in other ways? What do you do for work?
I work in IT, in a software company. Lots of sitting, lots of deadlines. Last month we had a release, so I was in office until very late almost every day.
That would take it out of anyone. And who do you live with?
With my husband and his parents, and my daughter. Joint family only. It is nice, but also, no privacy, so sometimes I don't want to tell anybody anything.
Hm, I can imagine. I'm glad you came in then. Let me read your numbers from today first.
Your blood pressure is 118 over 76, and your pulse is 78 beats per minute.
Is that okay? I always think my BP will be high, because I get nervous in clinics.
That's a very comfortable reading, you don't need to worry about it. Now, with bleeding between periods there are a few possible reasons, and I don't want to guess from the history alone.
So what will you do? Will I need an operation?
Nothing like that. What I'd like to do first is arrange an ultrasound scan of your pelvis, to look at the womb and the ovaries properly.
Scan only? That is not painful, no? My cousin had one and she said they put something inside.
There are two ways of doing it, and the sonographer will tell you which suits you. For you, a scan over the tummy is likely to be enough. It's not painful, and it takes about twenty minutes.
Okay, okay. When can I do it?
The front desk will give you the first available slot, probably this week. Until then, I'd like you to note down on your phone the date of each bleed, how heavy it is, and any pain.
That I can do, I already keep my period dates in an app.
Perfect, then it's just adding a few lines. Bring it along when you come back.
And when will I see you again?
Let's say in ten days. By then the scan report will have reached me and we'll go through it together.
Ten days, okay. Doctor, one more question. Should I avoid anything until then, or can I carry on as usual?
Nothing to avoid. Carry on as normal, and if anything changes, you know where I am.
Thank you so much, doctor. And sorry again for the late, I will leave early next time only.
Take care. See you in ten days.
